CAMPUS GRAPH (Member A)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# info
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

CAMPUS GRAPH (Member B)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Representation
The campus is stored as an undirected, unweighted graph in the CampusGraph
class. Buildings are vertices, kept in a vector in buildings.txt order.
Walkways are edges, kept in an adjacency list (a vector of vectors of integer
indexes). Each building's list holds its neighbors in the order the
connections were accepted. Neighbors are never sorted, so BFS order is
predictable.

Why an adjacency list
A campus has only a few walkways per building, so the graph is sparse. An
adjacency list stores only the edges that exist, grows with the data (no fixed
size), and keeps neighbor insertion order. A matrix would waste space and would
not preserve neighbor order.

Edges and validation
Each accepted connection is added to both buildings' lists and counted once.
A connection is rejected if a name is empty, a building is unknown, a building
is connected to itself, or the connection already exists (including reversed
duplicates such as A|B and B|A). Building lookup trims whitespace and ignores
capitalization, and the spelling from the first accepted record in
buildings.txt is kept.

BFS reachability
BFS uses a std::queue and a visited vector. A building is marked visited when
it is added to the queue. A distance vector records the number of connections
from the start building. The output lists reachable buildings in visit order
with their distances, then "Reachable: X of Y". The start building has
distance 0 and counts as reachable. An unknown start prints an error, and an
isolated start prints only itself.

Loading
loadBuildings and loadConnections read each file with getline, skip blank and
comment lines, and trim whitespace and \r. For each rejected record they print
a warning with the filename, line number, and reason, then continue. A file
that cannot be opened prints an error and is treated as empty. Each loader
ends with a summary line of accepted and rejected counts. addBuilding and
addConnection return false and fill an error string, so the loader decides how
to print the message.

Reuse
The same graph is used for display, counts and degrees, and BFS, and later
(Final) for shortest path and the connectivity report.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

CAMPUS GRAPH (Member C)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Representation
The department hierarchy is stored as a general tree in the DepartmentTree
class. Each DepartmentNode holds its name, a pointer to its parent (null for
the root), and a vector of child pointers kept in insertion order. The
tree keeps a root pointer and a node count.

Why a vector of child pointers
A department can have any number of sub-departments, so a fixed number of
child slots would not work. A vector grows with the data (no fixed limit)
and keeps sibling order, which the traversals rely on.

Adding and validation
The first valid record is the root and must use NONE as its parent. Every
later department must name a parent that was accepted earlier. A department
is rejected if its name is empty, its parent is unknown, or its name already
exists ignoring capitalization. Lookups trim whitespace and ignore case, and
the spelling from the first accepted record is kept. A rejected addition
leaves the tree unchanged.

Traversals
Preorder visits a node and then its children. Postorder visits the children
and then the node. Level-order uses a std::queue and visits siblings in
insertion order. The hierarchy display is a preorder walk that indents four
spaces per depth level.

Statistics
Depth is the number of edges from the root (root depth 0). Height is the
maximum depth, computed with a queue. A leaf is a node with no children.
An empty tree reports 0 departments, 0 leaves, and height N/A. A root-only
tree has 1 department, 1 leaf, and height 0.

Loading
loadDepartments reads departments.txt with getline, skips blank and
comment lines, and trims whitespace and \r. For each rejected record it
prints a warning with the filename, line number, and reason, then
continues. A file that cannot be opened prints an error and is treated as
empty. The loader ends with a summary line of accepted and rejected counts.
addRoot and addChild return false and fill an error string, so the loader
decides how to print the message.

Memory
The DepartmentTree destructor deletes every node using an explicit stack, so
no heap memory is leaked and long chains cannot overflow the call stack.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
